setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Its Device page is open, so the header reads CH01, and Device shows CC Device, Mosaic's built-in generic MIDI device. Channel 2 is not set up yet. Both channels run at the default clock Rate /1 (one step per sixteenth note).
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). The Device page stays open but now reads CH02 and Device shows None: channel 2 has no output yet, and setting up channel 1 did not change it. The channel buttons choose which channel the screen edits.
steps.title: An unused channel has no output

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1). The header returns to CH01 and Device shows CC Device again: each channel keeps its own device.
steps.title: Return to channel 1

steps.caption: Device was the first of a channel's own settings; Rate is the second. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Clock and press K3. The Clock page for CH01 shows Rate /1, the default: one step per sixteenth note. Rate divides the clock, so /2 will run half as fast and make each step twice as long.
steps.title: Open the Clock page

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). The Clock page stays open and now reads CH02, with its own Rate /1.
steps.title: Select channel 2

steps.caption: Turn E3 down two detents to Rate /2 and press K3 to apply. Channel 2 now runs at half the speed of channel 1: each of its steps lasts two sixteenth notes.
steps.title: Give channel 2 a different rate

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1). Its Clock page still reads Rate /1: changing channel 2's rate left channel 1 alone.
steps.title: Channel 1 keeps its rate

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1) again. Its Clock page reads Rate /2. Each channel remembers its own settings, so channels can run at different speeds against one tempo.
steps.title: Channel 2 remembers its rate

steps.caption: Open the Device page for channel 2, give it its own MIDI output, give it pattern 1 with the range steps 1-4 and open its Clock page again. Select channel 1 and press Play. Channel 1 plays one note every sixteenth note; channel 2 plays one note every two sixteenth notes, so its notes are twice as far apart. Look at the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step", where the second port's notes arrive at half the pace of the first. Press Play again to stop.
steps.title: Hear channel 2 at half speed

title: Each channel keeps its own device and rate
